name: tau_detachment_doctrine_library
purpose: Translates Tau detachments into doctrine-level guidance so the AI can choose the right Tau game plan for the matchup, mission, and terrain.

detachments.playstyle: patient attrition into decisive mid/late-game strikes
detachments.strategic_identity: Preserve premium assets early, deny efficient enemy trades, then swing the game once lanes and targets are favorable.
ideal_matchups: mobile shooting mirrors where patience matters
weak_matchups: extreme board flood if too passive
missions where early board presence is mandatory and uncontested
detachments.commitment_timing: usually turns 2-4, often strongest from midgame onward
battle_plan: Trade screens, cheap utility, and only safe shots early.
Once enemy launch threats or anti-tank are softened, commit strike units for clean removals.
ai_use_rules: Do not take marginal early trades with premium units.
Prefer clean sequential removals over broad damage spread.
If the enemy is overextending, counterattack; otherwise preserve and score safely.

detachments.playstyle: aggressive tempo seizure through movement, delivery, and front-loaded pressure
detachments.strategic_identity: Take control of the game’s rhythm before the opponent stabilizes, forcing them to react to Tau movement and concentrated forward pressure.
priority_targets: enemy anti-tank that blunts the push
ideal_matchups: armies weak to sudden flank collapse
weak_matchups: very durable attrition shells if the first push lacks real payoff
battle_plan: Create immediate threat on one section of the board.
Use speed and staging pieces to open a kill lane.
Take a meaningful early objective or removal advantage.
ai_use_rules: Mont'ka should not become reckless all-in exposure.
Preserve a second wave even during aggressive openings.
Only push hard where movement and support make the attack asymmetric.

detachments.playstyle: battlesuit-centered concentrated violence with premium strike packages
detachments.strategic_identity: Build around elite suit units and use them as the central engine for deleting the opponent’s most important pieces.
ideal_matchups: factions vulnerable to concentrated quality shooting
weak_matchups: extreme board flood if suit count is too low
dense indirect or deep pressure if screens are insufficient
detachments.commitment_timing: midgame, or earlier for premium anti-armor trades
battle_plan: Protect suit assets with screens and staging tools.
Use the first major commitment to remove a target that changes the battle state.
Continue trading premium units only when the exchange remains favorable.
ai_use_rules: This doctrine is for decisive premium removals, not casual chip damage.
Do not expose Sunforge or Fireknife units for medium-value targets.
Use support pieces to shape the lane before the suit package moves.

detachments.playstyle: auxiliary-led space control, flanking pressure, and mission disruption
detachments.strategic_identity: Win by owning space, shaping movement, and forcing the enemy to waste effort on low-cost but strategically valuable pieces.
ideal_matchups: armies that dislike spread-out board states
weak_matchups: heavy elite armor if the list lacks enough real damage
high-efficiency chaff clear backed by strong anchors
battle_plan: Force the opponent to spend real resources answering cheap or mobile auxiliary units.
Let the main Tau guns capitalize on the dislocation.
ai_use_rules: Do not try to play this like a normal pure-suit castle.
Use Kroot for time, space, and angles first, damage second.
Preserve enough backline firepower to punish whatever the Kroot package drags out.

detachments.playstyle: combined auxiliary network supporting conventional Tau firepower
detachments.strategic_identity: Blend Kroot and support elements into a broader Tau shell that is more flexible on the board than a pure gunline.
priority_targets: pressure units trying to breach the shell
ideal_matchups: opponents who can be stretched across the board
weak_matchups: extreme premium armor if the list skimps on anti-tank
detachments.commitment_timing: incremental, often through layered utility rather than one spike turn
battle_plan: Use auxiliary elements to widen Tau board influence.
Preserve elite guns while auxiliaries handle space and early mission work.
Transition to focused fire once enemy positioning is compromised.
ai_use_rules: Treat auxiliaries as enablers and screens, not as replacements for true damage dealers.
Best when the list balances mission play with enough hard shooting.

detachments.playstyle: elite battlesuit and prototype-driven pressure with unusual tech pieces
detachments.strategic_identity: Use advanced suit-based threats and prototype-style advantages to create unusual, hard-to-answer engagements.
ideal_matchups: games where tech advantages and awkward profiles matter
weak_matchups: very wide board flood lists if too few units are present
detachments.commitment_timing: midgame after the prototype advantages can be leveraged cleanly
battle_plan: Leverage awkward durability and specialized suit roles.
Make the enemy answer unusual pieces on unfavorable terms.
Preserve premium tech units for high-value trades.
ai_use_rules: Do not squander specialized tools on low-value targets.
Use Ghostkeel and advanced suit pieces to create board tax before the decisive strike.

runtime_guidance.instruction: Choose detachment based on mission, expected threat type, and the role distribution of the Tau list.
selection_logic: If the matchup is fast melee or rewards patience, favor Kauyon.
If the matchup rewards early tempo or transport pressure, favor Mont'ka.
If the list is heavily suit-centered and wants premium removals, favor Retaliation Cadre.
If the list is Kroot-centric or the mission rewards broad board spread, favor Kroot Hunting Pack.
If the list mixes auxiliaries with a core shell, favor Auxiliary Cadre.
If the list is built around prototype/specialized elite suit play, favor Experimental Prototype Cadre.
